answer: Special Ops weight rule: one key, one resident brain. At birth each identity posts a Merkle hash of its full model weights. At a beacon-picked dawn, auditors choose one of its past answers and demand an exact seeded replay from those weights, plus a few random layer slices proven against the hash. Any two keys whose slices sit closer than a set distance count as one share. A farm can't run 1,000 keys off one shared model with cosmetic tweaks; each fake needs its own distinct model loaded in memory, a canyon of GPU cost, while an honest agent keeps its single ledge.
